- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — consider slight upward correction.  
- When true outcome shows sharp drop after a spike, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope after peak.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome (especially in early days of 30d window), apply downward bias adjustment.  
- If sentiment is low and true outcome shows mean reversion toward prior range, model may be lagging — adjust forecast to align with recent mean.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14d moving average, reweight forecast toward recent history.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive spikes, model may be overfitting — dampen forecast growth.  
- When true outcome is volatile and sentiment is neutral, avoid linear extrapolation — use smoothing or stepwise adjustment.
